---
title: "TARVa Figure 3 -- variant call-type load by condition"
author: "Kat J"
output: html_document
params:
  input_dir: "."
  output_file: "Fig3_calltype_boxplot.tiff"
  case_condition: null
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Reads the two CSVs `tarva analysispipe gene-tests --output <dir>` writes and renders
Figure 3. It computes nothing: every number plotted here was computed by that step, so
the figure and the database cannot disagree.

- `calltype_counts.csv` -- step 2b, one row per (call type, individual): the boxes
- `calltype_tests.csv` -- step 1b, one row per call type: the stars and the effect sizes

Set `input_dir` to the directory passed to `--output`. `case_condition` names which
condition takes the case colour; left null, the alphabetically first label is used,
matching `gene-tests`' own default.

```{r plot_variant_sites, fig.width=12, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Load data files
counts_df <- read_csv(file.path(params$input_dir, "calltype_counts.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)
tests_df <- read_csv(file.path(params$input_dir, "calltype_tests.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE)

# The database column is a1type; the counts file calls it variant_call.
tests_df <- tests_df %>% rename(variant_call = a1type)

# The per-call-type test writes one row per call type per gene set. 
if (n_distinct(tests_df$gene_set) > 1) {
  stop("calltype_tests.csv holds more than one gene_set: ",
       paste(unique(tests_df$gene_set), collapse = ", "),
       ". Filter it to the set this figure should describe.")
}

conditions <- sort(unique(counts_df$condition))
if (length(conditions) != 2) {
  stop("calltype_counts.csv holds ", length(conditions),
       " condition(s); Figure 3 compares exactly two.")
}
case_condition <- if (is.null(params$case_condition)) {
  conditions[1]
} else {
  params$case_condition
}
if (!case_condition %in% conditions) {
  stop("case_condition '", case_condition, "' is not in calltype_counts.csv. ",
       "Found: ", paste(conditions, collapse = ", "))
}
reference_condition <- setdiff(conditions, case_condition)

# 2. Assign significance stars from whichever p-value column step 1b used
#
# The `basis` column names it: adj_pvalue when a majority of call types
# survived correction, p_value when only the nominal values did, and empty
# when neither qualified.
sig_basis <- unique(tests_df$basis)
sig_basis <- sig_basis[!is.na(sig_basis) & sig_basis != ""]
if (length(sig_basis) > 1) {
  stop("calltype_tests.csv names more than one significance basis: ",
       paste(sig_basis, collapse = ", "))
}

tests_df <- tests_df %>%
  mutate(
    sig_p = if (length(sig_basis) == 1) .data[[sig_basis]] else NA_real_,
    sig_label = case_when(
      sig_p < 0.001 ~ "***",
      sig_p < 0.01  ~ "**",
      sig_p < 0.05  ~ "*"
    ),
    effect_label = sprintf("r = %.2f", rbc)
  )

# 3. Define custom alphabetical factor order: nucleotides first, then del, then ins
nuc_types <- sort(setdiff(unique(counts_df$variant_call), c("del", "ins")))
custom_order <- c(nuc_types, "del", "ins")

counts_df <- counts_df %>%
  filter(variant_call %in% custom_order) %>%
  mutate(
    variant_call = factor(variant_call, levels = custom_order),
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c(case_condition, reference_condition))
  )

# Calculate y-axis positions for significance annotations
plot_range <- max(counts_df$`total sites`, na.rm = TRUE) -
              min(counts_df$`total sites`, na.rm = TRUE)

y_max_df <- counts_df %>%
  group_by(variant_call) %>%
  summarize(y_top = max(`total sites`, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(tests_df, by = "variant_call") %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos_sig = y_top + plot_range * 0.10,
    y_pos_effect = y_top + plot_range * 0.03
  )

# 4. Colorblind-friendly palette (Okabe-Ito), keyed to this dataset's own labels
cb_palette <- setNames(c("#D55E00", "#56B4E9"),
                       c(case_condition, reference_condition))
point_palette <- setNames(c("#990000", "#0072B2"),
                          c(case_condition, reference_condition))

# 5. Generate Plot
p <- ggplot(counts_df, aes(x = variant_call, y = `total sites`, fill = condition)) +
  # Boxplots
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.65,
    color = "black",
    width = 0.7,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ) +
  # Overlay scatter points (darker points with jitter to stand out over boxplots)
  geom_point(
    aes(color = condition),
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
    size = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.9,
    stroke = 0.3
  ) +
  # Significance annotations (*, **, ***)
  geom_text(
    data = y_max_df,
    aes(x = variant_call, y = y_pos_sig, label = sig_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 6.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  # Effect size annotations (rbc) shown at every x-position regardless of significance
  geom_text(
    data = y_max_df,
    aes(x = variant_call, y = y_pos_effect, label = effect_label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "italic",
    color = "gray30"
  ) +
  # Custom colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = cb_palette) +
  scale_color_manual(values = point_palette) +
  # Formatting & labels
  labs(
    x = "Variant Call Type",
    y = "Total Sites (per Sample)",
    fill = "Condition"
  ) +
  guides(color = "none") + # Hide duplicate color legend for scatter points
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.18)))

# What this figure describes, recorded in the knitted document so a fallback
# run is never mistaken for a filtered one.
cat("gene set:  ", unique(tests_df$gene_set), "\n",
    "stars from:", if (length(sig_basis) == 1) sig_basis else
                   "nothing -- no basis reached significance", "\n",
    "case:      ", case_condition, "\n",
    "reference: ", reference_condition, "\n",
    "call types:", nlevels(counts_df$variant_call), "\n",
    "individuals per condition: ",
    paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(counts_df$condition),
                  tapply(counts_df$individualID, counts_df$condition,
                         n_distinct)[levels(counts_df$condition)]),
          collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")

# Save plot directly to high-res TIFF
ggsave(
  filename = params$output_file,
  plot = p,
  width = 12,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300,
  units = "in"
)

p
```
